items.passage: Transcript: Hi everyone, this is Nadia Quispe from the student elections committee. Campaigning for the council election opens Monday, so here is what you need to know about posters. Each candidate gets ten, and each one still needs our stamp before it goes up. Stamping usually happens at our office in Room 238, but that room is holding ballot boxes this month, so come to Room 115 in Larchmont Hall instead, Tuesday or Thursday afternoon. Bring a few extra copies. We keep one of every design on file, in case anyone complains later about what a poster said. Now, unstamped posters. In past years, our volunteers simply took them down. This year we are leaving them up, but each one we find counts as one of your ten, whether you put it up or a friend did. There is no warning first, and no stamping it afterward. Questions? Call extension 3052.
items.prompt: [Announcement — Student elections committee] Why does the speaker say, "Bring a few extra copies"?
choices: To let the committee keep a record of each design
To let volunteers replace any torn-down posters
To let candidates swap in new posters each week
To let the committee hand some out at the ballot boxes
items.correct_answer: To let the committee keep a record of each design
items.explanation: Right after the line the speaker says, "We keep one of every design on file, in case anyone complains later about what a poster said," so the extra copies are for the committee's record. "To let volunteers replace any torn-down posters" is wrong: the speaker never mentions replacing damaged posters, and volunteers take posters down only in the past-years description. "To let candidates swap in new posters each week" is wrong: nothing is said about weekly swaps; each candidate simply has ten. "To let the committee hand some out at the ballot boxes" is wrong: the ballot boxes are only why Room 238 is unavailable.
